channel.title: Home Poker Ledger — guides
channel.description: Short guides on running and settling a home poker game.

item.title: The bank came up short after poker night — who pays?
item.description: The chips do not match the money. How to find the cause, and who should absorb it once you have genuinely looked.

item.title: Running a home poker game with beginners at the table
item.description: How to include someone who has never played without slowing the game to a crawl or taking all their money in an hour.

item.title: How to be the banker at a home poker game
item.description: Running the money at a home poker game: collecting buy-ins, never banking from your own pocket, and cashing out in the right order.

item.title: Blinds and starting stacks for a home poker game
item.description: Picking blinds that fit your buy-in, why 100 big blinds is the usual starting stack, and how blind levels work if you are running a tournament.

item.title: Cash game or tournament for a home poker game?
item.description: The difference, which suits which group, and why the money side differs far more than the poker does. Includes the compromise most regular games settle on.

item.title: How to cash out at the end of a home poker game
item.description: The order to count a table down in, why you colour up before counting, and how to catch a count that does not match the money that went in.

item.title: Poker chip values and starting stacks — Home Poker Ledger
item.description: How to pick chip denominations that fit your buy-in: the 1:40 ratio, why three colours beats five, which colours to avoid, and how many chips you need.

item.title: Who deals at a home poker game, and how the button moves
item.description: Rotating the deal versus a dedicated dealer, how the button and blinds move, and the small mistakes that cause most home-game disputes.

item.title: How to find players for a home poker game
item.description: Where home game players actually come from, how to vet someone you do not know, and why the first invitation matters more than the rest.

item.title: How to run your first home poker game — Home Poker Ledger
item.description: Everything a first-time host needs in order: choosing stakes, how many players, what to buy, the rules to agree before dealing, and how to settle up at the end.

item.title: Home poker house rules — what to agree before the first hand
item.description: The short list a home game actually needs settled in advance: money rules, table rules, and who has the final say when something is disputed mid-hand.

item.title: How many poker chips do you need for a home game?
item.description: How many chips a home game needs by player count, why 500 is the usual answer, and which denomination always runs out first.

item.title: How many players for a home poker game?
item.description: Why six to eight is the sweet spot for a home game, how table size changes the way it plays, and what to do when ten people say yes.

item.title: Why home poker games die, and how to keep yours going
item.description: The four reasons a regular game quietly stops happening, and the handful of habits that keep one running for years.

item.title: How to pay up after a home poker game: cash, Venmo, IOUs
item.description: How the money actually moves once the ledger is settled: why fewer payments is better, cash versus transfer apps, rounding, and what to do about what is still owed.

item.title: Should you rake a home poker game?
item.description: Why taking a cut of the pot changes what your game is, what it costs the table over a season, and fairer ways to cover pizza and cards.

item.title: Poker rebuys, add-ons and late entries — Home Poker Ledger
item.description: What to agree before the first hand, how to record a rebuy so it survives to settlement, seating a late player, and cashing out early without breaking the count.

item.title: Why your poker settlement doesn't add up: five causes
item.description: The five errors that turn a five-minute settle into a forty-minute argument at a home poker game, and how to catch each one before money moves.

item.title: Side pots: when someone is all in for less
item.description: What happens to the betting when a short stack is all in, how to build the side pot without losing track, and the one rule that settles every dispute.

item.title: Tracking results across a season of home poker games
item.description: How to keep a record across weeks without it becoming a chore, what is worth recording, and why settling every night beats carrying balances forward.

item.title: Someone can't pay after a home poker game: what to do
item.description: How to prevent the most uncomfortable moment a home game produces, what to do when it happens anyway, and why making the numbers fit is the worst option.
